Fazle Karim Biswas & Others
full_judgment: 2. Facts leading to this appeal in short are that the land described in the schedule to the plaint belonged to the plaintiffs Fazle Karim Biswas and Nasim Biswas. They took loan of Tk. 200/00 from the defendant Jaha Baksha, a village money lender and as security of the loan mortgaged the suit land with him and as a token of that mortgage he obtained a patta from the plaintiff dated 9-3-53 (Ext. A), according to the local custom on an oral agreement that the defendant will reconvey the land when the plaintiff would pay back the loan. It was further stipulated in that agreement that the land will remain with the plaintiff (lessor) and half of the produce of the suit land would be paid to the defendant (lessee) by way of interest of the loan till the loan is repaid. The plaintiff possessed the land and paid half of the barga crops as per term of the agreement to the defendant for quite a number of years till 1953. Thereafter the property was put to auction by the landlord for arrears of rent due from the plaintiff as tenant. The plaintiff filed a Misc. case being Misc. case no. 344/45 and got the sale set aside and since then the plaintiff continued to remain in his possession all these years and continued to pay half the produce of the suit land as per the oral agreement but the defendant in violation of the agreement for reconveyance inspite of plaintiff's demand for the same after tendering the loan money, forcibly entered into the disputed land and dispossessed the plaintiff on 12-3-58 Hence the suit for Specific Performance of Contract and recovery of khas possession.
